how_to_edit: This is the ONLY place that names non-Claude models. Skills, agents and docs refer to kinds (trivial, scout-light, ...) and never to a model. A route is one way to reach a model: {router, id}. Routes inside a model are tried in order, free ones first. Edit a pick list when your data or decision changes; run `node tools/worker.mjs route` to check the result and `node tools/worker.mjs doctor` to see which routes can run on this machine. Routes marked "verified": false carry provisional model ids: check them against the provider's model list. Each change gets one line in `changelog` below. A router of type `cli` describes a command-line harness by data (bin, args, writeArgs, placeholders); docs/providers.md explains the fields.

openrouter.free: only :free models: 20 requests a minute and 50 a day, or 1,000 a day once the account has bought 10 USD of credits

codex.free: uses the Codex allowance of your ChatGPT plan; no API key
codex.note: OpenAI Codex CLI. The operating system enforces the sandbox: read-only (with web search) for scouts, writes confined to --dir for builders. It runs with your own Codex config (on Windows the sandbox setting lives there). About 20 to 50 s per call.

hermes.install: install Hermes Agent, then `hermes model` to sign in to Nous Portal
hermes.free: the free models of Nous Portal (they rotate); 50 requests a minute
hermes.note: Nous Hermes Agent as a text-only worker: one harmless toolset, no terminal and no file tools, so it cannot write. Files named with --files are packed into the prompt. Nous may keep prompts unless Privacy Mode is on.

glm-flash.good_at: EQ ('right-brained'): prose, UX copy, docs voice, naming, narrative, empathy, design critique

sub-orchestrator-sonnet.note: same job, for slices that need judgement

trivial.use_when: The brief holds all the input, or the answer is one stated fact: reformat a list, pull fields from pasted text, list or count files, find which files mention X, draft a commit message from a pasted diff. A wrong answer is cheap to spot.
trivial.not_for: anything that feeds a decision, or needs judgement

scout-light.use_when: Mere fact-finding: where is X, what value does Y hold, which files do Z. No high-quality reasoning needed.
scout-light.not_for: conflicting evidence, or any answer a decision hangs on

scout-deep.use_when: The answer feeds a decision, needs QA or reasoning, or evidence may conflict: log reading, inventories that must be complete, documentation lookups with sources.

test-writer.use_when: Writing the tests that define the pass condition, BEFORE the builder starts. Must be smarter than the builder, so two independent writers from different families both write tests from the spec only (never from the implementation); the lead merges them.
test-writer.after: Run `worker.mjs lock <test files>` before the builder starts and `worker.mjs verify` after. The builder's brief says: tests are read-only; a failing test means the code is wrong.

builder-iq.use_when: Correctness, structure and precision matter more than tone: code, scripts, configs, refactors, data transforms, algorithms.

builder-eq.use_when: The reader's experience matters more than the logic: UX copy, docs voice, narrative, naming, empathy, design critique.

review.rule: Every builder result gets a reviewer of the same tier and a different model family. Nice, not required: let EQ review IQ work and IQ review EQ work. The reviewer is read-only and receives the diff and the pass condition, never the builder's reasoning. The implementer never reviews its own work. A model from a third family may review instead: a sandboxed agent read-only in the worktree, or a text-only model that gets the diff and the pass condition packed with `worker.mjs ask <alias> <brief> --files <diff>`.

fallback_rules: Inside one pick: try its routes in order. A route is skipped at once when its key variable is unset or its program is not installed. A route fails on a non-zero exit, empty output, an error-looking answer, a timeout, a rate limit, or (write kinds) no changed file.
When every route of a pick fails: take the next pick in the list.

A pick that is a Claude agent cannot be run by worker.mjs. It prints the agent to spawn (exit code 3) and the caller spawns it with the model and effort stated in claude_agents. With --no-claude such picks are skipped.
When the last pick fails: go up exactly one tier (see the escalation rule in the lean-orchestrator skill).

2026-11-10: router type `cli` (a command-line harness described by data). Routers codex (GPT-6 Luna in an OS sandbox) and hermes (LongCat-2.5 on Nous Portal, text only). gpt-luna is a fallback before the Claude worker in scout-deep, builder-iq (max effort) and builder-eq; it is NOT a test writer, because its Intelligence Index (28 at max effort, lower at lower efforts) is below the builder it would check. longcat-free is a trivial fallback on a separate quota and an optional reviewer of a packed diff; its free offer is temporary.
